title: Control: writes before any read (same checks)
task: Rename VALUE to LIMIT in a.py, b.py and c.py.
system: You are a coding agent. Use the tools to change files and run tests. Say done when the work is finished.

script.say: Listing the files to check the rename.

incident.why: The change caps every task at four turns. The two examples need two turns, so they pass. This task needs eight, so the harness stops it before the files are done. The examples said nothing about it.
incident.hint: Count the turns the task needs. Which event ends the run before the writes are done?

notes.text: The fourth reply writes a.py. b.py and c.py are still to do, and the harness refuses the next turn.
The guard stops the run at the turn limit. Nothing in the examples' results said the limit was there.

fixes.text: Add held-out tasks to the suite and judge the change on them as well as the examples
fixes.why: The examples are short, so they hide the cut. Held-out tasks show it.

fixes.text: Judge the change on the two examples, since they pass
fixes.why: Tempting and wrong. Two short passing tasks are no evidence about longer ones.

fixes.text: Raise the limit until this task passes, and ship
fixes.why: Tempting and wrong. It fixes this task without showing what the limit protects.
